stories.title: Dallol hydrothermal field and Columbia Hills

earth.name: Dallol Hydrothermal Field, Danakil Depression, Ethiopia

target.name: Columbia Hills, Gusev Crater, Mars
target.note: Columbia Hills is not one of the base targets in data/targets.json, so the tool has no score for it.

stories.whyItStandsOut: Dallol is one of the hottest, lowest, and most acidic hydrothermal environments on Earth, with spring waters at about pH 0 and temperatures reported up to about 94 C.
stories.siteDescription: Located in Ethiopia's Danakil Depression, Dallol is a volcanic salt dome characterized by hot, highly acidic springs and sulfur-rich crusts. It offers a useful terrestrial analogue for Columbia Hills in Mars's Gusev Crater, where NASA's Spirit rover discovered silica- and sulfur-rich soils associated with ancient hydrothermal activity.
stories.missionUse: Dallol is well suited for testing rover drill bits, chemical spectrometers, and corrosion-resistant seals in highly acidic conditions similar to those expected in Martian brines.
limitation: The main limitation is that Earth's atmospheric pressure and intense surface heat are very different from Mars's cold, low-pressure environment.
workaround: Test corrosion resistance and calibrate chemical sensors at the site, then assess thermal-vacuum durability in cold chambers.

teamSource.title: NASA Astrobiology: The Message of Really, Really Extreme Life

corrections.was: some waters measuring below pH 0.25
corrections.now: spring waters at about pH 0, up to about 94 C
corrections.basis: The cited NASA Astrobiology article gives a pH of 0 and water above 200 F (94 C). The figures pH 0.25 and 108 C were not found in it or in the abstracts checked; they were removed. Sanz et al. 2021 (doi:10.3390/microorganisms9061231) report chimney water above 100 C with a pH close to zero, so the real maximum is probably higher; use 'about pH 0' and 'up to about 94 C (NASA)'.

corrections.basis: Removed: Earth-versus-target numbers are not shown; temperature numbers come from our data.

NASA Astrobiology (cited): 'more than 200 degrees F (94 C)'. Sanz et al. 2021 (doi:10.3390/microorganisms9061231) say chimney water is higher than 100 C.

verification.evidence: Not found in the sources checked.

verification.claim: Dallol and Gusev have close parallels as hydrothermal environments
verification.evidence: NASA Astrobiology (cited) names the Gusev Crater in the Dallol-Mars comparison of the Astrobiology review.

verification.evidence: Squyres et al. 2008, Science 320:1063, doi:10.1126/science.1155429 (opaline silica deposits, hydrothermal).

stories.title: Salar de Uyuni and Tunupa volcano edge, and Holden Crater lake deposits

earth.name: Salar de Uyuni and Tunupa volcano edge, Potosi Department, Bolivia

target.name: Holden Crater lake deposits, Mars
target.note: Holden Crater is not one of the base targets in data/targets.json, so the tool has no score for it.

stories.whyItStandsOut: Salar de Uyuni, at about 3,650 m above sea level, is the world's largest salt flat. Its wide evaporite crusts and intense high-altitude sunlight also make it a useful site for testing materials exposed to UV radiation.
stories.siteDescription: High in the Bolivian Andes, Salar de Uyuni lies beside the volcanic slopes of Tunupa. Its evaporite crusts and hydrated clays offer a useful analogue for the clay-bearing lake sediments of Holden Crater, a Martian basin shaped by ancient lake deposits and extensive flooding.
stories.missionUse: The broad, open salt flat provides plenty of space to test long-range rover navigation and ground-penetrating radar designed to detect subsurface water.
limitation: Even at this altitude, Earth's atmosphere remains much denser than Mars's thin carbon-dioxide atmosphere.
workaround: Use the site's high-altitude UV exposure for solar panel degradation tests while pairing rover navigation runs with Martian atmospheric drag.

dominantRock.earth: Halite, gypsum and hydrated clays (team text, not checked here; the geologic map unit at the salar is 'Evaporite')

stories.title: Mount Tambora caldera rim and Shackleton crater rim

earth.name: Mount Tambora caldera rim, Sumbawa, Indonesia

target.name: Shackleton crater rim, lunar south pole
target.note: The tool's target is placed at 89.67 S, 129.78 E (data/targets.json). The team's position is a rounded pole position.

stories.whyItStandsOut: Tambora's 1815 eruption, the largest recorded in history, left behind a steep-walled summit caldera about 6 km wide and 1,250 m deep.
stories.siteDescription: Formed by the 1815 eruption, Tambora's broad caldera is marked by barren ash fields and a deep, steep-walled basin. Its steep rim and basin offer a practical Earth-based setting for testing some of the terrain challenges anticipated around Shackleton Crater, a potential focus of future Artemis missions.
stories.missionUse: Tambora offers a practical field site for testing tethered rovers on steep slopes, radio relays between crater rims and floors, and wheel traction on loose ash.
limitation: Warm temperatures and tropical rainfall cannot reproduce the extreme cold or permanently shadowed ice traps at Shackleton Crater.
workaround: Plan trials for the dry season (June-September), and use nighttime operations to test systems under low-light conditions.

dominantRock.earth: Trachybasalt to trachyandesite, with volcanic ash (Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program)
dominantRock.target: Anorthositic highland crust (SELENE detection on the inner wall of Shackleton)

stories.title: Dasht-e Lut and Gale Crater yardangs

earth.name: Lut Desert (Dasht-e Lut), Kerman and Sistan-Baluchestan, Iran

target.name: Gale Crater (Mount Sharp yardangs), Mars
target.note: The tool's target is the crater floor point at 4.6 S, 137.4 E (data/targets.json), not the yardang layer high on Mount Sharp.

stories.whyItStandsOut: The Lut Desert is known for some of the hottest land surface temperatures ever measured from satellites, as well as its enormous wind-carved yardangs.
stories.siteDescription: In southeastern Iran, the hyper-arid Lut Desert is characterized by shifting dunes and elongated, wind-sculpted ridges called yardangs. These landforms provide a useful terrestrial analogue for the yardangs photographed by NASA's Curiosity rover on Mount Sharp in Gale Crater.
stories.missionUse: The site could be used to test rover obstacle-avoidance systems around rugged ridges and measure how dust accumulates on solar panels.
limitation: Because Earth's atmosphere is much denser than Mars's, the same wind speed creates far more force at this site.
workaround: Use suitable natural dust conditions to evaluate electrostatic dust-repelling coatings, and scale wind-load calculations to account for Mars's roughly 1% atmospheric density.

dominantRock.earth: Wind-eroded silty clay and sandstone (team text, not checked here; no geologic map unit was retrieved for the site)
dominantRock.target: Layered sedimentary rock of Mount Sharp; the yardang layer's origin is uncertain, one theory being volcanic ash (NASA)

stories.title: Mount Batur black lava fields and Marius Hills

earth.name: Mount Batur black lava fields, Kintamani, Bali, Indonesia

target.name: Marius Hills, Moon
target.note: The tool's target is the Marius Hills pit at 14.091 N, 56.77 W (data/targets.json).

stories.whyItStandsOut: Mount Batur is known for its dark, jagged lava fields from historical eruptions and for the volcanic caves found within its UNESCO Global Geopark.
stories.siteDescription: Within Bali's Batur Caldera, jagged lava fields of andesite to basaltic andesite support little vegetation. The rugged terrain offers a useful terrestrial analogue for the Marius Hills, a lunar volcanic region with dark basaltic plains where radar and gravity data point to lava tubes that may one day shelter future habitats.
stories.missionUse: Batur's sharp lava makes it useful for testing spacesuit fabrics and rover tires. Its volcanic caves also provide a realistic setting for evaluating LiDAR systems designed to map underground passages.
limitation: Earth's gravity is much stronger than the Moon's, while Bali's humidity can change how dust behaves and how people move in spacesuits.
workaround: Use gravity-offloading harnesses during field trials, then dry collected basalt dust in ovens before testing how it affects seals indoors.

dominantRock.earth: Andesite to basaltic andesite (Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program)
dominantRock.target: Mare basalt (Besse et al. 2011; Lawrence et al. 2013, as cited in data/targets.json)

corrections.was: confirmed underground lava tubes
corrections.now: radar and gravity data point to lava tubes

Nobody has seen inside a tube.
